finding: Three explicit endpoint root-ratio inequalities analytically exclude all three previously allowed five-positive-frequency phase words. Subject to the named unreviewed phase and root-order imports, every strict negative-coordinate certificate for any box satisfying the three tests needs at least six distinct positive finite frequencies, irrespective of endpoint atoms. One full-width box around (s+1)^7 with radius 9/10 independently satisfies the tests; its 28 corner minors and rational root-bracket checks were replayed exactly. This is conditional and does not rule out six or more frequencies or solve the original decision.
additional_findings: Two explicit stable full-width septic boxes and their convex hull have one independently certified common numerator, while their coefficientwise interval hull contains a corner with strictly negative sixth Hurwitz determinant. This is an obstruction to replacing nonrectangular stable families by their independent hull.

For a separate stable box and its explicit endpoint neighborhood, a four-atom exact certificate excludes every nonnegative combination of the midpoint and its seven derivatives; every common monic numerator must have some coefficient less than -1/160 in its midpoint derivative basis. A different unrestricted common numerator exists.
remaining_gap: The full original arbitrary stable septic box decision remains open. The ratio theorem is conditional, and its phase classification and root-order prerequisites are author candidates awaiting independent whole-scope review.
next_action: Try to remove or weaken the ratio hypotheses or address six-node and higher strict certificates with new mathematical constraints.
